name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
note: Saint Lucia's sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers', the jurisdiction's own sheet, with an Inland Revenue Department officer as its contact), read 2026-10-30. The TIN is a numeric code issued to individuals and entities upon application, generated by the system in sequential order and used for all tax types; it isn't issued automatically, but assigned when the person applies for registration or on third-party information that they should be registered. So `when` is application and `who` anyone (the sheet sets no citizenship or residence). Structure: 'a maximum of six (6) digits', so the form takes one to six digits (no fewest is stated; being sequential from one, the fewest is read as one digit). A tax account number joins the TIN to a two-digit tax-type code (its example: TIN 1234, VAT account 123427), not held. The sheet says TINs are used only for tax and customs, not that anything needs one, so `needed` is left out. No check, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Saint Lucia: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: The TIN is a numeric code which is issued to individuals, and entities upon application. The codes are generated by the system, in sequential order, and once issued are used by a person for all tax types. ... TINs are not issued automatically in this jurisdiction ... The TIN consists of a maximum of six (6) digits.
